defects.title: The optional input basis is ignored
defects.trigger: [v, basis] = LP7(J, model, LPproblem, epsilon); LP7(J, model, LPproblem, epsilon, basis)
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-23, gurobi) line 58 sets basis = [] before the solve, so the input basis never reaches solveCobraLP (lines 73-74 unreachable); the optimum is unchanged
defects.expected: the basis used to warm-start the LP, as the help text says, or the help text saying it is ignored

notes: No testLP7.m and no legacy test calling LP7 alone. Same pattern and same cosmetic basis defect as LP3 (testLP3.m). Exemptions: 70 (condition ends with && 0), 73-74 (basis cleared on line 58), 83 (solveCobraLP always returns a basis field). Gurobi returns no point for an infeasible LP, so v = NaN (line 97); glpk returns a nonempty x for the same infeasible LP (origStat 110), so the NaN assertion is gurobi-only. Hand-derived expectations on the 2-metabolite/4-reaction network of testLP3, plus a C*v <= d row capping z (v4 = 2 with epsilon 3). The model input is unused by LP7 (line 37 commented out).

No testBlocked.m; testQFCA.m uses a variable named blocked, not the function. Hand-derived blocked sets on three small networks (dead end: x = [-1 -1], objective -2; none blocked; one dead-end branch: x4 = -1), certificate checked against S'*u <= x. Solver argument: [] and the legacy names gurobi/linprog/cplex use the configured COBRA solver (line 47); 'glpk' takes line 50 (explicit solveCobraLP solver). Lines 56-57 exempt as unreachable: the LP always has the feasible point 0 and is bounded (objective only on x in [-1, 0]). Test placed in testSWIFTCORE (holds testSWIFTCORE.m and testPartition.m).

defects.title: The weights of reversible and irreversible reactions are given to the wrong reactions
defects.trigger: an irreversible weighted reaction placed before a reversible weighted one with another weight: m.S = sparse([1 -1 -1]); m.rev = [0; 0; 1]; m.lb = [0; 0; -10]; m.ub = [10; 10; 10]; rng(0); core(m, [0; 0; 0], [0; 10; 1], 'gurobi')
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-23, gurobi) flux = [1 1 0]: the flux leaves through R2 (weight 10) instead of R3 (weight 1). Line 36 orders the penalty variables [reversible weighted; irreversible weighted], lines 39-41 pair the i-th penalty variable with the i-th weighted reaction in model order; with R2 reversible and R3 irreversible (weights [0; 1; 10]) the cheaper R2 is correctly chosen
defects.expected: each reaction penalised by its own weight: flux = [1 0 1]

defects.title: An infeasible LP ends with MATLAB's unassigned-output error
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-23, gurobi) warning "Optimization was stopped with status 0", then 'Output argument "flux" (and possibly others) not assigned a value'
defects.expected: an error naming the cause (the LP status) or an output marking the failure

notes: Reproduction (MATLAB, gurobi as LP solver): m.S = sparse([1 -1 -1]); m.rev = [0; 0; 1]; m.lb = [0; 0; -10]; m.ub = [10; 10; 10]; rng(0); core(m, [0; 0; 0], [0; 10; 1], 'gurobi') -> [1 1 0] (expected [1 0 1]); m2 = m; m2.rev = [0; 1; 0]; core(m2, [0; 0; 0], [0; 1; 10], 'gurobi') -> [1 1 0] (correct, R2 is the cheap one). Quarantine reach: confined to weight vectors whose nonzero weights differ between reversible and irreversible reactions with an irreversible weighted reaction before a reversible weighted one in model order (equal nonzero weights are unaffected). The only caller is swiftcore (lines 114, 130), which passes the user weights; its reduction step (line 95) sums the weights of merged reactions, so non-uniform weights arise even from uniform input. swiftcore callers: createTissueSpecificModel (options.weights), swiftGapFill. LEAD DECISION: seed core -> swiftcore. The solver input of core is unused (always the configured COBRA LP solver).
confirmed_by: lead (read the code: line 36 orders the objective weights reversible first, then irreversible, while lines 39-41 pair the auxiliary variables with reactions in model order (temp1(weights~=0,:)), so with interleaved reversible and irreversible reactions the weights land on other reactions; default seed: swiftcore passes the user's weights)

notes: Tier 1 in the test (the ledger lists Tier 3): hand-built 7-metabolite/8-reaction model, no solver; the function only changes bounds (findOrganicExRxns and findRxnsFromMets default form call no solver). Expected bounds derived by hand: organic exchanges written "met ->" get lb 0, those written "-> met" get ub 0 (both close uptake; the comment of line 55 says "secretion", misleading but harmless), biomass, functionToKeep, inorganic and notMediumConstrained reactions and medium exchanges keep their bounds. Sections cover notMediumConstrained empty/nonempty and a medium with/without exchange reaction. No warnings are raised (a biomass reaction is given and no formula has X/Y).

defects.title: The positions of the second reaction of each pair are not returned
defects.trigger: any call of findMustLL that finds a set (AntCore setup of the OptForce tutorial)
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-23, gurobi) 687 sets found with excludedRxns = the EX_* reactions; posMustLL(:, 2) is 0 for every set: the second assignment repeats the first (column 1)
defects.expected: posMustLL(i, :) holds the positions of both reactions of row i (help text: number of sets x 2)

defects.title: The documented default of excludedRxns (empty) is a function handle, so a call without it stops
defects.trigger: findMustLL(model, minFluxesW, maxFluxesW, 'constrOpt', constrOpt, 'printLevel', 0, 'printExcel', 0) without excludedRxns, with or without 'printReport', 0, 'keepInputs', 0
defects.observed: (R2025a, 2026-11-23) report on: "Brace indexing is not supported for variables of this type." in the report loop; report and inputs off: "Input A of class cell and input B of class function_handle must be the same class, unless one is double." in intersect. Line 159 passes the validation function as the default value
defects.expected: excludedRxns defaults to empty (help text "Default: empty")

notes: No testFindMustLL.m; testOptForce.m calls findMustLL once (tutorial setup, with excludedRxns, outputs not asserted) but tests optForce, so a new quarantine-layout file was written. Reproduction (MATLAB): model = getDistributedModel('AntCore.mat'); model.c(strcmp(model.rxns,'R75')) = 1; lb of EX_gluc, EX_o2, EX_so4, EX_nh3, EX_cit, EX_glyc = -100; model = changeObjective(model,'EX_suc'); [minW, maxW] = FVAOptForce(model, struct('rxnList',{{'R75'}},'rxnValues',14,'rxnBoundType','b'), struct('rxnList',{{'R75','EX_suc'}},'rxnValues',[0,155.55],'rxnBoundType','bb')); constrOpt = struct('rxnList',{{'EX_gluc','R75','EX_suc'}},'values',[-100,0,155.5]'); [s, p] = findMustLL(model, minW, maxW, 'constrOpt', constrOpt, 'excludedRxns', model.rxns(contains(model.rxns,'EX_')), 'printLevel', 0, 'printExcel', 0) -> p(:,2) all 0; omitting 'excludedRxns' -> error. Run in a temporary folder (it writes run folders). Quarantine reach: no src caller of findMustLL (only testOptForce and the tutorial), so the seed is NONE. The UL run took about 12 minutes (58 sets): a future test needs a smaller model or a restrictive excludedRxns. Same two defects in all three findMust* (LL/UL/UU); findMustL/findMustU (BLOCKED rows) use the same addParamValue('excludedRxns', <validator>) pattern and should be checked when unblocked.
confirmed_by: lead (read the code: line 159 addParamValue('excludedRxns', <validator>) makes the validator the default value, so a call without excludedRxns stops; lines 297-298 assign column 1 twice and never column 2 of the position output; no src caller)
